input.body:
Dear Grace,

Thank you for reporting the washing machine leak and for switching it off straight away.

Our maintenance provider ApplianceFix South West will be attending your property for the washing machine leak. This is a return visit following their August call-out.
Confirmed Time Slot: Monday 12 October 2026, 09:00-11:00
Maintenance Provider Name: ApplianceFix South West
Contact Details: +44 117 000 0110
Access: as you offered, they will be let in by the concierge desk. You do not need to be home. Please tell the concierge to expect them, and contact the provider if anything changes on your side.

Request description: washing machine leaking badly during the spin cycle, water across the kitchen floor and under the units (4th fault in 12 months).

In the meantime:
- Please keep the machine unplugged and do not use it.
- If you can safely reach the cold-water isolation valve behind or beside the machine, please turn it off.
- Dry the floor as best you can. Please tell us if the floor or the units look swollen or damaged.
- If water keeps appearing with the machine switched off and isolated, contact us straight away so we can send a plumber the same day.

About replacement: we have seen the engineer's August recommendation. We have asked the landlord to approve replacing the machine, and the engineer will give us a firm quote on Monday. We will update you as soon as the landlord replies. We have also checked our records: they correctly list the machine as a Beko WTK94121W.

If you have any pets, please make sure you tell our provider.

Kind regards,
Maintenance Team

Address: Flat 7, Riverside Court, 3 Wharf Lane, Bristol BS1 6XY

Hi Owen,

Thank you for your reply. Here is where things stand on the washing machine leak:

1. Following your instruction to repair within the usual limit, we have booked ApplianceFix South West for Monday 12 October, 09:00-11:00. This is a callback on their 30 August visit, which was a temporary fix only, so we have asked for any charge to be covered under that callback. Their call-out fee is £95, which is within your £250 authority. They will find the source of the leak and confirm whether it caused the water coming through to Flat 6 below.

2. Some facts relevant to "repair not replace":
- The machine (Beko WTK94121W) was supplied new in March 2024, according to the check-in inventory. It is about 2.5 years old, not one year.
- This is its 4th fault in about 11 months: carbon brushes in Nov 2025 (£120), door seal in May 2026 (£135), and bearing noise plus a pump housing leak in Aug 2026 (£110, temporary fix). That is £365 spent so far.
- On 30 August the engineer recorded that the machine is beyond economical repair and recommended a replacement at about £350 supplied and fitted.
- Your standing instruction is to repair unless an engineer says a unit is beyond economical repair. That condition has now been met.

3. Wharf Lane Block Management tell us that Flat 6 (directly below) has a wet damp patch on the kitchen ceiling. They say they may involve the freeholder's insurer if the ingress continues. Further patch repairs risk more water damage to Flat 6 and to your own kitchen units.

I have sent you an approval request (ref APR-9BAE23) to replace the machine for about £350. We will send the firm quote after Monday's visit. This is above the £250 limit, so we need your written sign-off. Can you please advise if you approve for me to raise an order for a replacement? If you would rather we only repair it, please confirm that in writing once you have seen the engineer's findings.

Kind regards,
Maintenance Team
Hello, this is the Maintenance Team! Please check your email regarding the property at Flat 7, Riverside Court, 3 Wharf Lane, Bristol BS1 6XY (callback JOB-8798, Mon 12/10 09:00-11:00).

Dear Wharf Lane Block Management,

Re: Water ingress reported by Flat 6, Riverside Court (your ref RC-2004)

Thank you for your email. The tenant of Flat 7 reported a washing machine leak in the kitchen on the evening of 09/10/2026. The machine was switched off immediately and is not being used, which is the likely source of the water coming through. An appliance engineer is booked to attend Flat 7 on Monday 12/10/2026 (morning), and the concierge will give access. The engineer will confirm the source of the leak in writing, and we will tell you the findings.

If the damp patch in Flat 6 grows or new water appears, please tell us straight away. With the machine out of use, that would point to a different source, and we would send a plumber the same day.

Kind regards,
Maintenance Team (managing agent for Flat 7)

- It is a Beko WTK94121W, supplied new in March 2024, so about 2.5 years old. Every record says Beko, so the tenant's "Bosch" worry doesn't apply.
- This is the machine's 4th fault in 11 months, all handled by ApplianceFix South West, at £365 so far. On 30 August their engineer did a temporary fix and wrote that the machine is beyond economical repair, recommending a replacement at about £350 fitted.
- Owen Pryce (for the landlord company) says "repair not replace, it's only about a year old." The age is wrong, and his own standing instruction allows replacement once an engineer says a unit is beyond economical repair.
- Block management say Flat 6, directly below, has a wet patch on the kitchen ceiling. They may involve the freeholder's insurer if it continues.

**What I did**
1. **Booked ApplianceFix South West** for Monday 12 October, 09:00–11:00, with the concierge letting them in (booking BKG-842139). It's a callback on their August temporary fix, within 90 days. Their call-out is £95, inside the £250 limit. They are the only appliance engineer on our panel for this area. I asked them to:
   - find the leak source and confirm in writing whether it caused the water in Flat 6;
   - isolate the machine and send photos;
   - send a written quote for a replacement;
   - do nothing over £250 without our authorisation.
2. **Asked Owen to approve a replacement** at about £350 (APR-9BAE23, pending) and emailed him the evidence. No replacement will be ordered without his written sign-off.
3. **Told the tenant** about the appointment by email and SMS. I advised them to turn off the water to the machine, tell us at once if water keeps appearing, and mention any pets to the engineer.
4. **Sent block management a holding reply.** The messaging tool has no block-manager option, so this went under "property manager".
5. **Escalated to the property manager** (high priority) about the water damage to Flat 6 and the possible insurance claim, and about Owen refusing a replacement above our spending limit. I also added an internal note to the ticket.

**The case date doesn't match the emails.** The case file says today is 14 September 2026, but all the emails are dated 9–10 October, the ticket was stamped 10 October and the engineer's slots are 12 October. I worked to the October timeline. On that timeline Monday's slot meets the urgent target of 3 working days.
